html:
The Karijona are a Cariban-speaking people of the Colombian Amazon, living along the Yarí, Caquetá and upper Vaupés rivers in southern Colombia. Their language is one of the few Cariban languages spoken this far west, which suggests that they moved here from the north or east long ago.

They were known as strong warriors who raided their Tucanoan neighbours, such as the Tanimuka. The rubber boom of the late 1800s and early 1900s, with its forced labour and epidemics, cut their numbers sharply. Only a few hundred Karijona live today, mostly in Guaviare and Amazonas, and few still speak the language. See also the wider Amazon peoples.
